memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a date dimension (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: GlobalMart has two date dimensions, and choosing the wrong one silently changes the answer.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a date dimension

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a date dimension (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Use `transaction_date` for operational questions: daily sales, footfall, stock movement. It is when the transaction happened.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a date dimension

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a date dimension (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Use `fiscal_date` for anything compared against a budget or reported by period, because the fiscal year does not start in January.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a date dimension

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a date dimension (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: When a question says "last quarter" in a financial context it means a fiscal quarter, so group by `fiscal_date`.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a date dimension

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a revenue metric (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Three metrics have "revenue" in the name and they are not interchangeable.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a revenue metric

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a revenue metric (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Use `metric_l1_total_net_revenue` by default. Net revenue is after returns and discounts.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a revenue metric

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a revenue metric (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: `metric_l1_sql_margin_bridge_gross_revenue` is gross, before returns and discounts. It exists for the margin bridge and is the wrong figure elsewhere.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a revenue metric

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Choosing a revenue metric (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: `metric_l1_sql_net_sales_summary_net_revenue` agrees with total net revenue but is scoped to its own SQL dataset's grain, so it does not slice by every dimension.
memoryItems.title: Choosing a revenue metric

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: GlobalMart's metrics are layered, and the layer is in both the metric id and its tags, L1 through L5.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: L1 metrics (`metric_l1_*`) are base aggregations over a single fact column. They are the only layer that touches a fact directly.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: L2 metrics (`metric_l2_cross_*`) are ratios between two L1 metrics, such as order count over net revenue.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: L3 metrics (`metric_l3_*`) apply a filter to an L1 or L2 metric, usually a WHERE on a dimension attribute such as channel type.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: L4 and L5 metrics compose further on top of the lower layers.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

memoryItems.description: GlobalMart metric conventions › Metric layers (compiled from docs/knowledge/metric-hierarchy.md)
memoryItems.instruction: Prefer the lowest layer that answers the question. Total net revenue is an L1 metric; net revenue for one channel is an existing L3 metric, not an L1 metric with a filter added.
memoryItems.title: Metric layers

metrics.description: Shows the total number of spend records by summing the Spend Count from the Daily Campaign Spend dataset, reflecting how many daily spend entries are included for the selected filters and time period.
metrics.title: Total Spend Count (Daily Campaign Spend)

metrics.description: Counts the total number of display ad impressions by summing the underlying Impression Count from the Display Impression data. Use it as a core volume metric when evaluating campaign performance across sites, audiences, or time periods.
metrics.title: Total Impression Count (Display Impression)

metrics.description: Sums the Email Open “Open Count” fact to show the total number of email opens, used as an overall engagement volume indicator across campaigns, audiences, or time periods.
metrics.title: Total Open Count (Email Open)

metrics.description: Total number of emails sent, calculated by summing the Send Count measure from the Email Send data. Use this metric to track overall send volume and to break it down by time, campaign, or audience segments.
metrics.title: Total Send Count (Email Send)

metrics.description: Shows total spend on paid search clicks by summing Click Cost across all Paid Search Click records, within the current report scope (such as selected time period or campaign filters).
metrics.title: Total Click Cost (Paid Search Click)

metrics.description: Tracks total paid search click volume by summing the Click Count from the Paid Search Click dataset. Use it to monitor overall click trends and performance in paid search reporting.
metrics.title: Total Click Count (Paid Search Click)

metrics.description: Sums Spend to show total marketing/campaign spend in the Campaign ROI data. Use it to track and compare overall spending across campaigns, time periods, or other business segments.
metrics.title: Total Spend (Campaign ROI)

metrics.description: Sums daily recorded Spend amounts to show total marketing campaign spend. Use this metric to monitor and compare overall spend across reports and time periods based on the Daily Campaign Spend data.
metrics.title: Total Campaign Spend

metrics.description: Compares total campaign spend to the total number of daily spend records by calculating the difference between Spend and Spend Count. Use it to spot potential logging gaps or anomalies where the amount spent and the number of recorded spend entries don’t align for the selected period and filters.
metrics.title: Campaign Spend vs Spend Count (Daily Campaign Spend) Change

metrics.description: Compares activity volume by calculating the difference between the count of Daily Campaign Spend records and the total Email Send count for the current filters and time period. Use it to see whether spend record volume is higher or lower than email sending volume, and by how much.
metrics.title: Spend Count (Daily Campaign Spend) vs Send Count (Email Send) Change

metrics.description: Shows the net difference between total emails sent and total email opens for the current filters and time period. Use it to quantify how many more sends occurred than opens (or vice versa) when analyzing email volume versus engagement.
metrics.title: Send Count (Email Send) vs Open Count (Email Open) Change

metrics.description: Shows the net difference in engagement volume by subtracting total paid search clicks from total email opens for the same slice of data. Use it to see whether email opens are higher or lower than paid search clicks and by how much.
metrics.title: Open Count (Email Open) vs Click Count (Paid Search Click) Change

metrics.description: Shows the difference between total paid search clicks and total display ad impressions. Use it to compare click volume against impression volume and monitor shifts in performance between these two channels over time or across segments.
metrics.title: Click Count (Paid Search Click) vs Impression Count (Display Impression) Change

metrics.description: Shows the net difference between total display ad impressions and total paid search click spend within the current report scope (for example, a selected time period or campaign). Use it to compare display impression volume against paid search costs in a single number and see how the gap shifts as you filter or segment the data.
metrics.title: Impression Count (Display Impression) vs Click Cost (Paid Search Click) Change

metrics.description: Shows the net difference between total paid search click costs and total campaign spend for the current analysis scope (such as selected campaigns or time periods). Use it to identify whether click-level costs are running above or below overall budget/spend and by how much.
metrics.title: Click Cost (Paid Search Click) vs Spend (Campaign ROI) Change

metrics.description: Total marketing campaign spend filtered to the In-Store sales channel. Use this metric to track and compare in-store campaign investment over time or alongside spend from other channels.
metrics.title: Campaign Spend — In-Store Channel

metrics.description: Total marketing campaign spend filtered to the Online sales channel. Use this metric to isolate and compare online-only spending versus overall campaign spend across reports and time periods.
metrics.title: Campaign Spend — Online Channel

metrics.description: Total marketing campaign spend filtered to the North region. Use this metric to track and compare campaign spending in North across reports and time periods.
metrics.title: Campaign Spend — North Region

metrics.description: Counts the number of daily campaign spend records for the In-Store sales channel. Use it to monitor how much In-Store spend activity is being logged over the selected time period and any applied filters.
metrics.title: Spend Count (Daily Campaign Spend) — In-Store Channel

metrics.description: Counts the number of daily campaign spend records for the Online sales channel, showing how many Online spend entries are captured within the selected time period and filters. Use it to monitor record volume/completeness for Online campaign spend activity.
metrics.title: Spend Count (Daily Campaign Spend) — Online Channel

metrics.description: Counts the number of daily campaign spend records for the North region. Use it to monitor activity volume in North and to compare record counts across time periods or against other regions when filters change.
metrics.title: Spend Count (Daily Campaign Spend) — North Region

metrics.description: Counts the total number of emails sent that are associated specifically with the In-Store sales channel. Use this metric to monitor and compare In-Store email send volume over time or across campaigns and segments.
metrics.title: Send Count (Email Send) — In-Store Channel

metrics.description: Counts the total number of emails sent for the Online sales channel. Use this metric to monitor online email send volume and compare it across time periods or against other channels.
metrics.title: Send Count (Email Send) — Online Channel

metrics.description: Counts the total number of emails sent for the North region. Use this metric to monitor and report North’s email sending volume across dashboards and reports.
metrics.title: Send Count (Email Send) — North Region

metrics.description: Counts the total number of email opens, limited to the In-Store sales channel. Use it to monitor and compare email engagement volume for In-Store activity versus other channels.
metrics.title: Open Count (Email Open) — In-Store Channel

metrics.description: Counts the total number of email opens for activity limited to the Online sales channel. Use it to monitor and compare email engagement volume for Online versus other channels or overall opens.
metrics.title: Open Count (Email Open) — Online Channel

metrics.description: Counts the total number of email opens for the North region only. Use this metric to track email engagement volume in the North and compare it with other regions or with overall open counts.
metrics.title: Open Count (Email Open) — North Region

metrics.description: Counts paid search clicks limited to the In-Store sales channel, so you can track click volume specifically attributable to in-store activity. Use it to compare In-Store paid search performance against overall paid search click totals.
metrics.title: Click Count (Paid Search Click) — In-Store Channel

metrics.description: Counts paid search clicks limited to the Online sales channel, helping you monitor click volume and trends specifically for online performance. Use it in reports and dashboards when you need online-only paid search click activity rather than total clicks across all channels.
metrics.title: Click Count (Paid Search Click) — Online Channel

metrics.description: Counts total paid search clicks for the North region only. Use it to track paid search click volume and trends for North in regional performance reporting.
metrics.title: Click Count (Paid Search Click) — North Region

metrics.description: Counts total display ad impressions specifically for the In-Store sales channel. Use this metric to monitor in-store impression volume and compare it to impression counts for other channels over the same period.
metrics.title: Impression Count (Display Impression) — In-Store Channel

metrics.description: Counts total display ad impressions for the Online sales channel only, using the core Display Impression impression count metric and filtering Channel Type to Online. Use this metric to track online display impression volume when comparing performance by audience, site, or time period.
metrics.title: Impression Count (Display Impression) — Online Channel

metrics.description: Total number of display ad impressions, filtered to the North region. Use this metric to monitor and compare impression volume specifically for North-focused reporting across campaigns, audiences, or time periods.
metrics.title: Impression Count (Display Impression) — North Region

metrics.description: Total spend on paid search clicks, limited to the In-Store sales channel. Use this metric to track click cost for in-store activity within the currently selected time period or campaign scope.
metrics.title: Click Cost (Paid Search Click) — In-Store Channel

metrics.description: Total paid search click spend attributable to the Online sales channel, calculated by summing click costs within the current reporting scope (for example, selected time periods or campaign filters). Use this metric to monitor and compare online paid search costs across segments and over time.
metrics.title: Click Cost (Paid Search Click) — Online Channel

metrics.description: Total paid search click spend filtered to the North region. Use this metric to monitor how much is being spent on paid search clicks in North and compare performance across time periods or against other regional metrics.
metrics.title: Click Cost (Paid Search Click) — North Region

metrics.description: Total campaign spend filtered to the In-Store sales channel within the Campaign ROI context. Use it to analyze and compare in-store marketing spend across campaigns, time periods, and other segments.
metrics.title: Spend (Campaign ROI) — In-Store Channel

metrics.description: Total campaign spend limited to the Online sales channel. Use it to track and compare online campaign spending across time periods, campaigns, or other Campaign ROI breakdowns.
metrics.title: Spend (Campaign ROI) — Online Channel

metrics.description: Total campaign spend limited to the North region. Use this metric to monitor and compare how much is being spent on campaigns specifically within the North area.
metrics.title: Spend (Campaign ROI) — North Region

metrics.description: Tracks the month-over-month change in campaign spend for the In-Store sales channel, comparing the current month’s spend to the prior month. Use it to see whether in-store campaign investment is increasing or decreasing over time.
metrics.title: MoM: Campaign Spend — In-Store Channel

metrics.description: Shows the month-over-month change in marketing campaign spend for the Online sales channel, comparing the current month’s spend with the previous month. Use it to track whether online campaign investment is increasing or decreasing over time.
metrics.title: MoM: Campaign Spend — Online Channel

metrics.description: Shows the month-over-month change in marketing campaign spend for the North region by subtracting the prior month’s spend from the current month. Use it to monitor how North’s campaign spending is trending and identify increases or decreases from one month to the next.
metrics.title: MoM: Campaign Spend — North Region

metrics.description: Tracks the month-over-month change in the count of daily campaign spend records for the In-Store sales channel by comparing the current month to the previous month. Use it to monitor whether the volume of logged In-Store spend activity is trending up or down over time.
metrics.title: MoM: Spend Count (Daily Campaign Spend) — In-Store Channel

metrics.description: Measures the month-over-month change in the number of daily campaign spend records for the Online channel by subtracting last month’s count from the current month’s count. Use it to track whether the volume of Online spend entries is increasing or decreasing from one month to the next.
metrics.title: MoM: Spend Count (Daily Campaign Spend) — Online Channel

metrics.description: Year-over-year percentage change in Campaign Spend for the In-Store sales channel, comparing the current period to the prior year. Use this metric to understand how in-store campaign investment is trending annually.
metrics.title: YoY: Campaign Spend — In-Store Channel

metrics.description: Measures the year-over-year percentage change in Campaign Spend for the Online sales channel by comparing the current year’s spend to the previous year.
metrics.title: YoY: Campaign Spend — Online Channel

metrics.description: Measures the year-over-year percentage change in Campaign Spend for the North region by comparing the current year’s spend to the previous year. Use it to track how marketing campaign spending in North is growing or declining over time.
metrics.title: YoY: Campaign Spend — North Region

metrics.description: Measures the year-over-year percentage change in the number of daily campaign spend records for the In-Store channel, comparing the current period against the same metric in the prior year. Use it to see whether In-Store spend activity volume is trending up or down versus last year.
metrics.title: YoY: Spend Count (Daily Campaign Spend) — In-Store Channel

metrics.description: Year-over-year percent change in the count of daily campaign spend records for the Online channel. Use it to see how the volume of Online spend entries is trending versus the same period in the prior year.
metrics.title: YoY: Spend Count (Daily Campaign Spend) — Online Channel

attributes.description: Customer Name from the Customer dataset, used to identify, group, and filter analyses by individual customer.

attributes.description: Identifier for the customer’s lifecycle stage in the Customer dataset, used to group or filter customers by lifecycle stage.

attributes.description: Identifier for a customer’s loyalty tier in the Customer dataset. Use it to group or filter customers by loyalty tier.

attributes.description: Describes the customer segment in plain language for each record in the Customer Segment dataset. Use it to group and filter customers by segment description in reporting and analysis.

attributes.description: Customer Segment name used to categorize customers into segments for analysis. Use it to group or filter metrics by segment within the Customer Segment dataset.

attributes.description: Unique identifier for each marketing campaign in the Campaign ROI dataset, used to group, filter, and drill into ROI and performance metrics by campaign.
attributes.title: Campaign ID (Campaign ROI)

facts.description: Revenue amount attributed to a campaign, used to analyze campaign return on investment in the Campaign ROI dataset.
facts.title: Attributed Revenue (Campaign ROI)

facts.description: Total campaign spend recorded in the Campaign ROI dataset, used to analyze and aggregate marketing costs across campaigns.
facts.title: Spend (Campaign ROI)

sql.statement:
SELECT
    csd.campaign_id,
    csd.day AS campaign_date,
    SUM(csd.spend) AS total_spend,
    SUM(COALESCE(wol.revenue, 0)) AS attributed_revenue
FROM {{ datasource_schema }}.fact_campaign_spend_daily csd
LEFT JOIN {{ datasource_schema }}.fact_web_order_header woh ON csd.day = woh.order_date
LEFT JOIN {{ datasource_schema }}.fact_web_order_line wol ON woh.order_id = wol.order_id
GROUP BY 1, 2
